claim: Rab6-positive secretory vesicles are transported from the Golgi apparatus to the cell periphery by kinesin-1 KIF5B and kinesin-3 KIF13B.
source: Here, we show that Rab6-positive secretory vesicles are transported from the Golgi apparatus to the cell periphery by kinesin-1 KIF5B and kinesin-3 KIF13B, which determine the location of secretion events.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript including knockout and rescue experiments.

claim: KIF5B and KIF13B determine the location of secretion events.
source: Here, we show that Rab6-positive secretory vesicles are transported from the Golgi apparatus to the cell periphery by kinesin-1 KIF5B and kinesin-3 KIF13B, which determine the location of secretion events.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by data showing that in 4X-KO cells, exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi rather than distributed throughout the cell.

claim: KIF5B plays a dominant role in Rab6 vesicle transport.
source: KIF5B plays a dominant role, whereas KIF13B helps Rab6 vesicles to reach freshly polymerized microtubule ends, to which KIF5B binds poorly, likely because its cofactors, MAP7-family proteins, are slow in populating these ends.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by data showing that KIF5B knockout has a much stronger effect on vesicle motility than KIF13B knockout.

claim: KIF13B helps Rab6 vesicles to reach freshly polymerized microtubule ends.
source: KIF5B plays a dominant role, whereas KIF13B helps Rab6 vesicles to reach freshly polymerized microtubule ends, to which KIF5B binds poorly, likely because its cofactors, MAP7-family proteins, are slow in populating these ends.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by data showing that KIF13B-380-LZ-GFP is enriched at growing MT ends and that Rab6 vesicles are less efficient in reaching EB3-positive MT ends in KIF13B-KO cells.

claim: KIF5B binds poorly to freshly polymerized microtubule ends because its cofactors, MAP7-family proteins, are slow in populating these ends.
source: KIF5B plays a dominant role, whereas KIF13B helps Rab6 vesicles to reach freshly polymerized microtubule ends, to which KIF5B binds poorly, likely because its cofactors, MAP7-family proteins, are slow in populating these ends.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by data showing that MAP7 displays a delay in binding to freshly grown, EB3-positive MT ends and that KIF5B-560 is less abundant on EB3-positive MT ends.

claim: During microtubule plus-end directed transport, both KIF5B and KIF13B localize to the vesicle front and can be engaged on the same vesicle.
source: Sub-pixel localization demonstrated that during microtubule plus-end directed transport, both kinesins localize to the vesicle front and can be engaged on the same vesicle.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by sub-pixel localization data showing that both kinesins are enriched at the front of moving vesicles and can colocalize on the same vesicle.

claim: When vesicles reverse direction, KIF13B relocates to the middle of the vesicle, while KIF5B shifts to the back.
source: When vesicles reverse direction, KIF13B relocates to the middle of the vesicle, while KIF5B shifts to the back, suggesting that KIF5B but not KIF13B undergoes a tug-of-war with a minus-end directed motor.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by analysis of opposite polarity runs showing that the projected distance between KIF13B and Rab6 is close to zero for backward runs, while it is slightly negative for KIF5B.

claim: KIF5B but not KIF13B undergoes a tug-of-war with a minus-end directed motor.
source: When vesicles reverse direction, KIF13B relocates to the middle of the vesicle, while KIF5B shifts to the back, suggesting that KIF5B but not KIF13B undergoes a tug-of-war with a minus-end directed motor.
evidence: The abstract states this as a suggestion based on the observation that KIF5B shifts to the back of vesicles during direction reversal, which is supported by data and inference about motor behavior under load.

claim: KIF13B associates with Rab6-positive secretory vesicles.
source: To image secretory carriers, we used the small GTPase Rab6, which was shown to be a highly robust and ubiquitous marker of exocytotic vesicles (Fourriere et al., 2019; Grigoriev et al., 2007). In non-neuronal cells, Rab6 is represented by the Rab6A and Rab6A' isoforms that will be collectively called Rab6; in this study, the Rab6A isoform was used in all live imaging experiments. While testing colocalization of Rab6 vesicles with different kinesins, we found that KIF13B, as well as its motorless tail region, were abundantly present on Rab6-positive vesicles in both fixed and live HeLa cells (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: The text states this finding and refers to Figure 1A-D showing colocalization data.

claim: KIF13A displays little binding to Rab6 vesicles.
source: In contrast, its closest homologue KIF13A displayed little binding to Rab6 vesicles (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), in line with previous work showing that KIF13A specifically binds to recycling endosomes by associating with the Rab11 family members Rab11A, Rab11B and Rab25 (Delevoye et al., 2014).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing colocalization data, and cites previous work on KIF13A specificity.

claim: KIF13A specifically binds to recycling endosomes by associating with the Rab11 family members Rab11A, Rab11B and Rab25.
source: In contrast, its closest homologue KIF13A displayed little binding to Rab6 vesicles (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), in line with previous work showing that KIF13A specifically binds to recycling endosomes by associating with the Rab11 family members Rab11A, Rab11B and Rab25 (Delevoye et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Delevoye et al., 2014) for this claim.

claim: PAUF-positive carriers are labeled with Rab6.
source: We analyzed the colocalization between the CARTS cargo protein, PAUF-mRFP and Rab6 and found that they indeed colocalized both in fixed cells stained for endogenous Rab6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), and also in live cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: The text states this finding and refers to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1E showing colocalization data.

claim: Only a sub-population of Rab6-positive vesicles contained PAUF (~60% and 50% in fixed and live cells, respectively).
source: Only a sub-population of Rab6-positive vesicles contained PAUF (~60% and 50% in fixed and live cells, respectively) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text states this quantification and refers to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rab6 vesicles may serve multiple exocytotic routes, with PAUF utilizing one of these routes.
source: This suggests that Rab6 vesicles may serve multiple exocytotic routes, with PAUF utilizing one of these routes.
evidence: The text states this as a suggestion based on the observation that only a sub-population of Rab6 vesicles contain PAUF.

claim: Less than 20% of PAUF vesicles contained the classic secretion marker, the temperature-sensitive VSV-G.
source: In line with this view, in secretion assays, less than 20% of PAUF vesicles contained the classic secretion marker, the temperature-sensitive VSV-G (Wakana et al., 2012), while a high degree of colocalization of VSV-G and Rab6 has been observed (Grigoriev et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Wakana et al., 2012) for this claim.

claim: A high degree of colocalization of VSV-G and Rab6 has been observed.
source: In line with this view, in secretion assays, less than 20% of PAUF vesicles contained the classic secretion marker, the temperature-sensitive VSV-G (Wakana et al., 2012), while a high degree of colocalization of VSV-G and Rab6 has been observed (Grigoriev et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Grigoriev et al., 2007) for this claim.

claim: No colocalization between Rab6 and GFP-Eg5 was detected in both fixed and live cells.
source: Even though we were able to confirm that PAUF-positive carriers are labeled with Rab6, we could not detect any colocalization between Rab6 and GFP-Eg5, both in fixed and in live cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D), in contrast with a previous report (Wakana et al., 2013).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D, contrasting with a previous report.

claim: PAUF colocalized with KIF13B, as 50.7 ± 22.3% of PAUF-mRFP-positive vesicles were labeled with GFP-KIF13B.
source: However, PAUF colocalized with KIF13B, as 50.7 ± 22.3% of PAUF-mRFP-positive vesicles were labeled with GFP-KIF13B (determined from 10 cells), and kymograph analysis of PAUF/Rab6-positive vesicles clearly showed that they move together (Figure 1F).
evidence: The text states this quantification and refers to Figure 1F showing kymograph analysis.

claim: KIF13B persists on the vesicles until the actual fusion event takes place and then disappears together with the Rab6 signal.
source: Analysis of vesicle fusion with the plasma membrane by total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy (TIRFM) revealed that KIF13B persists on the vesicles until the actual fusion event takes place and then disappears together with the Rab6 signal (Figure 1G).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 1G showing vesicle fusion analysis.

claim: GFP-KIF13B does not exchange on exocytotic vesicles.
source: By performing fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) experiments, we observed that GFP-KIF13B does not exchange on exocytotic vesicles (Figure 1H), similar to what we have previously observed for Rab6 and Rab8 (Grigoriev et al., 2007; Grigoriev et al., 2011).
evidence: The text states this observation from FRAP experiments and refers to Figure 1H, citing previous work on Rab6 and Rab8.

claim: The motor KIF13B is stably bound to the vesicles, and its detachment is not required prior to vesicle fusion with the plasma membrane.
source: Our data indicate that the motor is stably bound to the vesicles, and its detachment is not required prior to vesicle fusion with the plasma membrane.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on FRAP data showing no exchange and fusion analysis showing persistence until fusion.

claim: The region including the MBS, a coiled-coil and the DUF3694 domains (607–1623) of KIF13B was necessary and sufficient for the binding to Rab6 vesicles.
source: The region including the MBS, a coiled-coil and the DUF3694 domains (607–1623) was necessary and sufficient for the binding to Rab6 vesicles, whereas the CAP-Gly domain and the motor domain were dispensable for the binding (Figure 1I,J).
evidence: The text states this finding from deletion mutant analysis and refers to Figure 1I,J.

claim: The CAP-Gly domain and the motor domain of KIF13B were dispensable for binding to Rab6 vesicles.
source: The region including the MBS, a coiled-coil and the DUF3694 domains (607–1623) was necessary and sufficient for the binding to Rab6 vesicles, whereas the CAP-Gly domain and the motor domain were dispensable for the binding (Figure 1I,J).
evidence: The text states this finding from deletion mutant analysis and refers to Figure 1I,J.

claim: All obtained kinesin knockout cell lines were viable and showed no proliferation defects.
source: We generated gene knockout cell lines lacking KIF5B, KIF13B, KIF5B and KIF13B together (KIF5B/KIF13B-KO), or KIF5B, KIF13B, KIF1B and KIF1C (4X-KO), and observed that the silencing of these kinesin genes led to the loss of the respective proteins (Figure 2A). All obtained cell lines were viable and showed no proliferation defects.
evidence: The text states this observation about the knockout cell lines and refers to Figure 2A showing Western blots.

claim: Different kinesin knockout cells could spread normally as formation of focal adhesions was not perturbed.
source: Different kinesin knockout cells could spread normally as formation of focal adhesions was not perturbed, though the total cell area showed some variability between different cell lines, possibly due to clonal effects (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B showing focal adhesion staining and cell area quantification.

claim: The MT cytoskeleton was somewhat less focused around the MT-organizing center in all cells lacking KIF5B.
source: The MT cytoskeleton was somewhat less focused around the MT-organizing center in all cells lacking KIF5B, whereas the staining for EB1 comets appeared normal (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A showing MT staining.

claim: Endosomes showed increased perinuclear clustering, particularly in the 4X-KO cells.
source: Endosomes showed increased perinuclear clustering, particularly in the 4X-KO cells, and their number appeared reduced in this cell line, although we cannot exclude that this effect was due to the fact that strongly clustered endosomes are more difficult to count (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C showing endosome staining and quantification.

claim: Mitochondria were shifted toward the perinuclear region in all cell lines lacking KIF5B.
source: Furthermore, mitochondria were shifted toward the perinuclear region in all cell lines lacking KIF5B (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D), as described previously (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Tanaka et al., 1998).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,D, citing previous work.

claim: The number of Rab6 vesicle runs was very similar in KIF13B-KO cells compared to control.
source: In KIF13B-KO cells, the number of vesicle runs was very similar to control.
evidence: The text states this observation, which is supported by quantification shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A very strong reduction in the number of runs was observed in the KIF5B-KO cells.
source: In contrast, a very strong reduction in the number of runs was observed in the KIF5B-KO cells.
evidence: The text states this observation, which is supported by quantification shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The double knockout of KIF5B and KIF13B (KIF5B/KIF13B-KO) had a synergistic effect, as the number of Rab6 vesicle runs was reduced compared to the single KIF5B-KO.
source: Interestingly, the double knockout of KIF5B and KIF13B (KIF5B/KIF13B-KO) had a synergistic effect, as the number of Rab6 vesicle runs was reduced compared to the single KIF5B-KO (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2C,D showing tracking and quantification.

claim: Both KIF5B and KIF13B cooperate in the transport of Rab6 vesicles, with KIF5B being the major player.
source: These results indicate that both kinesins cooperate in the transport of Rab6 vesicles, with KIF5B being the major player.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the synergistic effect of the double knockout and the stronger effect of KIF5B knockout alone.

claim: The 4X-KO cells did not show a stronger reduction in the number of runs compared to the double KIF5B/KIF13B-KO.
source: The 4X-KO cells did not show a stronger reduction in the number of runs compared to the double KIF5B/KIF13B-KO (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), suggesting that KIF1B and KIF1C are not sufficient for Rab6 vesicle transport.
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, drawing a conclusion about KIF1B and KIF1C.

claim: Expression of KIF5B in 4X-KO cells restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control.
source: Expression of KIF5B restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control, and the same was observed when KIF13B was re-expressed (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F showing tracking and quantification.

claim: Expression of KIF13B in 4X-KO cells restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control.
source: Expression of KIF5B restored the number of vesicle runs to values similar to control, and the same was observed when KIF13B was re-expressed (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F showing tracking and quantification.

claim: Simultaneous re-expression of KIF1B and KIF1C did not rescue Rab6 vesicle motility in 4X-KO cells.
source: Interestingly, simultaneous re-expression of KIF1B and KIF1C did not rescue Rab6 vesicle motility in 4X-KO cells (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F showing tracking and quantification.

claim: KIF1B and KIF1C were functional, as their expression could rescue the localization of Rab11-positive endosomes.
source: Importantly, these kinesins were functional, as their expression could rescue the localization of Rab11-positive endosomes: compared to control cells, the distribution of Rab11 carriers was strongly shifted toward the Golgi area in the 4X-KO cells, and this phenotype was reversed upon simultaneous re-expression of KIF1B and KIF1C (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 2D showing Rab11 localization analysis.

claim: Expression of Eg5 in the 4X-KO did not restore vesicle movement.
source: Furthermore, expression of Eg5 in the 4X-KO did not restore vesicle movement (Figure 2E,F), consistent with our observations that Eg5 does not localize to Rab6-positive vesicles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The text states this observation from rescue experiments and refers to Figure 2E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The number of vesicle runs was not affected by siRNA-mediated depletion of Eg5.
source: In agreement with these data, the number of vesicle runs was not affected by siRNA-mediated depletion of Eg5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: The text states this observation from siRNA experiments and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F.

claim: Eg5 and KIF1B/1C make no major contribution to the motility of Rab6 vesicles.
source: Thus, these data indicate that Eg5 and KIF1B/1C make no major contribution to the motility of Rab6 vesicles.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on rescue and knockdown experiments.

claim: The percentage of tracks containing runs was below 10% in all analyzed conditions.
source: We found that in all cases the percentage of tracks containing runs was below 10% (Figure 2G), and, as could be expected, it strongly correlated with the absolute number of vesicle runs (Figure 2D,F).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2G showing quantification.

claim: The fraction of processive movement inside the tracks that did contain runs remained almost the same for all conditions (on average, one third).
source: This was due to the fact that the fraction of processive movement inside the tracks that did contain runs remained almost the same for all conditions (on average, one third; Figure 2I).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2I showing distribution analysis.

claim: The duration of tracks that contained runs was consistently longer (on average, six times) than tracks without runs in all conditions.
source: In all conditions, the duration of tracks that contained runs was consistently longer (on average, six times) than tracks without runs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2—figure supplement 2G showing quantification.

claim: KIF5B and KIF13B drive a large fraction of processive movements of Rab6 vesicles but have no major impact on their diffusive motility.
source: Together, these data indicate that KIF5B and KIF13B drive a large fraction of processive movements of Rab6 vesicles but have no major impact on their diffusive motility.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the analysis of processive versus diffusive movements.

claim: The average Rab6 vesicle speed in KIF13B-KO cell clones and the mixed KIF13B-KO population was mildly but significantly reduced compared to control.
source: While the average Rab6 vesicle speed in KIF13B-KO cell clones and the mixed KIF13B-KO population was mildly but significantly reduced compared to control, the few Rab6 vesicles that still moved in the KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells displayed speeds much higher than those in control cells, an effect that was particularly obvious when speeds of all individual tracks rather than average velocities per cell were plotted (Figure 3A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A showing speed analysis.

claim: The few Rab6 vesicles that still moved in the KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells displayed speeds much higher than those in control cells.
source: While the average Rab6 vesicle speed in KIF13B-KO cell clones and the mixed KIF13B-KO population was mildly but significantly reduced compared to control, the few Rab6 vesicles that still moved in the KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells displayed speeds much higher than those in control cells, an effect that was particularly obvious when speeds of all individual tracks rather than average velocities per cell were plotted (Figure 3A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A showing speed analysis.

claim: Vesicles moving with speeds exceeding 3 μm/s were very rare in control cells but could be readily detected in KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells.
source: Interestingly, we observed the appearance of vesicles moving with speeds exceeding 3 μm/s, which were very rare in control cells but could be readily detected in KIF5B-KO, KIF5B/KIF13B-KO and 4X-KO cells (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B showing speed distributions.

claim: The residual, faster movements of Rab6 vesicles in cells lacking KIF5B and KIF13B could be driven by another kinesin or by dynein.
source: The residual, faster movements of Rab6 vesicles in cells lacking KIF5B and KIF13B could be driven by another kinesin or by dynein, as our previous work has shown that dynein-dependent Rab6 vesicle movements can occur with velocities of 2–4 μm/s (Schlager et al., 2014; Splinter et al., 2012).
evidence: The text states this interpretation and cites previous work on dynein-dependent movements.

claim: Run duration was relatively constant in all conditions.
source: We also analyzed other parameters of Rab6 vesicle motility, namely the duration and length of individual vesicle runs. We found that run duration was relatively constant in all conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B showing run duration distributions.

claim: Loss of KIF13B had no significant impact on run length.
source: Loss of KIF13B had no significant impact on run length, indicating that this motor does not significantly contribute to the processivity of vesicle movement driven by KIF5B.
evidence: The text states this observation and draws a conclusion about KIF13B's contribution to processivity.

claim: The residual runs observed in the absence of KIF5B were significantly longer than those in control cells.
source: Interestingly, the residual runs observed in the absence of KIF5B were significantly longer than those in control cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), possibly reflecting the strong sensitivity of this motor to obstacles (Telley et al., 2009).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, citing previous work on KIF5B sensitivity to obstacles.

claim: In most cases, the distributions of vesicle speeds matched much better the sum of two Gaussians than one Gaussian.
source: If only one motor were involved in vesicle movement, one Gaussian curve would be expected to fit the data. However, in most cases, the distributions of vesicle speeds matched much better the sum of two Gaussians (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C,D), indicating that there are at least two populations of vesicles with different average speeds per run.
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C,D showing speed distribution fits.

claim: There are at least two populations of vesicles with different average speeds per run.
source: If only one motor were involved in vesicle movement, one Gaussian curve would be expected to fit the data. However, in most cases, the distributions of vesicle speeds matched much better the sum of two Gaussians (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C,D), indicating that there are at least two populations of vesicles with different average speeds per run.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the two-Gaussian fit and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C,D.

claim: In control cells, there is a slower vesicle population with speed 1.20 ± 0.26 μm/sec and a faster one with a value of 1.71 ± 0.49 μm/s.
source: In control, there is a slower vesicle population with speed 1.20 ± 0.26 μm/sec (average ± SD), and a faster one with a value of 1.71 ± 0.49 μm/s (average ± SD) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Figure 3C,D).
evidence: The text states this quantification from Gaussian fits and refers to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Figure 3C,D.

claim: The fraction of higher speed runs was reduced in the clonal and mixed KIF13B-KO cells.
source: The fraction of higher speed runs was reduced in the clonal and mixed KIF13B-KO cells, while it was increased in the KIF5B-KO and KIF13B rescue of 4X-KO (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing Gaussian fit parameters.

claim: Rab6 vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued by expressing KIF13B moved significantly faster than those in cells rescued with KIF5B.
source: In contrast, Rab6 vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued by expressing KIF13B moved significantly faster than those in cells rescued with KIF5B (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing speed distributions.

claim: In cells rescued by expressing either KIF5B or KIF13B, vesicle tracks were distributed throughout the whole cytoplasm.
source: It is important to emphasize that in cells rescued by expressing either KIF5B or KIF13B, vesicle tracks were distributed throughout the whole cytoplasm (Figure 2E).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 2E showing tracking images.

claim: The observed difference in vesicle speeds could not be explained by differences in cell regions where the movement took place.
source: Thus, the observed speed difference could not be explained by differences in cell regions where the movement took place, such as cell thickness or interference with other organelles.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the observation that vesicle tracks were distributed throughout the cytoplasm.

claim: KIF13B is a faster motor compared to KIF5B.
source: However, the observed difference in vesicle speeds can be explained by previous observations showing that KIF13B is a faster motor compared to KIF5B (Arpağ et al., 2014; Norris et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Arpağ et al., 2014; Norris et al., 2014) for this claim.

claim: Single-molecule imaging of dimeric motor-containing fragments KIF13B-380-LZ and KIF5B-560 in 4X-KO cells confirmed that KIF13B moves significantly faster than KIF5B.
source: Indeed, single-molecule imaging of dimeric motor-containing fragments lacking the cargo binding tails, KIF13B-380-LZ and KIF5B-560, in 4X-KO cells confirmed that KIF13B moves significantly faster than KIF5B (Figure 3E).
evidence: The text states this observation from single-molecule imaging and refers to Figure 3E showing speed quantification.

claim: Peroxisome speed increased when the KIF5B:KIF13B plasmid ratio decreased in the FRB-FKBP chemical dimerization system.
source: We used different ratios of KIF5B and KIF13B-expressing plasmids as a way to manipulate the relative motor abundance on peroxisomes and observed that peroxisome speed increased when the KIF5B:KIF13B plasmid ratio decreased (Figure 3G,H), similar to what we described previously for KIF5B and KIF1A (Gumy et al., 2017).
evidence: The text states this observation from the peroxisome trafficking assay and refers to Figure 3G,H, citing previous work.

claim: When KIF5B and KIF13B were co-expressed on peroxisomes, intermediate velocities were observed, suggesting simultaneous engagement or very rapid switching between the two types of motors.
source: Kymographs of peroxisome movements showed that when the two kinesins were co-expressed, intermediate velocities were observed, suggesting simultaneous engagement or very rapid switching between the two types of motors (Figure 3G).
evidence: The text states this observation and interpretation from kymograph analysis and refers to Figure 3G.

claim: A significant excess of KIF13B-encoding plasmid was needed to shift peroxisome speeds to higher values.
source: Interestingly, a significant excess of KIF13B-encoding plasmid was needed to shift peroxisome speeds to higher values (Figure 3G,H), in agreement with in vitro gliding assays, which indicated that the slower kinesin-1 predominated when combined with kinesin-3 at a 1:1 molar ratio (Arpağ et al., 2014).
evidence: The text states this observation and refers to Figure 3G,H, citing previous in vitro work.

claim: Approximately 1–2 dimers of KIF5B-GFP and 3–5 dimers of GFP-KIF13B could be detected on the vesicles in 4X-KO rescue experiments.
source: We observed that approximately 1–2 dimers of KIF5B-GFP and 3–5 dimers of GFP-KIF13B could be detected on the vesicles (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: The text states this quantification from fluorescence intensity analysis and refers to Figure 4A,B.

claim: The maximum number of KIF5B binding sites on Rab6 vesicle is lower than that of KIF13B.
source: Since these experiments were performed with overexpressed full-length kinesins, these data suggest that the maximum number of KIF5B binding sites on Rab6 vesicle is lower than that of KIF13B.
evidence: The text states this interpretation based on the observation that fewer KIF5B molecules were detected on vesicles compared to KIF13B.

claim: In the endogenous situation the KIF13B abundance is likely low and the KIF13B binding sites are not saturated.
source: However, it is likely that in the endogenous situation the KIF13B abundance is low and the KIF13B binding sites are not saturated.
evidence: The text states this as a likely scenario to explain why overexpressed but not endogenous KIF13B can rescue vesicle motility.

claim: KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B could be present simultaneously on the same Rab6-positive vesicle.
source: Finally, we co-expressed KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B together and found that they could be present simultaneously on the same Rab6-positive vesicle (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: The text states this observation from co-expression experiments and refers to Figure 4E,F showing colocalization.

claim: In 4X-KO cells where KIF5B and KIF13B were expressed separately, mCherry-Rab6A vesicles bound to KIF5B-GFP moved slower than the ones bound to GFP-KIF13B.
source: In 4X-KO cells where the two kinesins were expressed separately, this analysis showed that mCherry-Rab6A vesicles bound to KIF5B-GFP moved slower than the ones bound to GFP-KIF13B, whereas in co-expressing cells, the particles associated with both motors had speeds that were intermediate between those of KIF5B and KIF13B (Figure 4F,G), in agreement with the data on the recruitment of these two motors to peroxisomes (Figure 3H).
evidence: The text states this observation from automated speed analysis and refers to Figure 4F,G and Figure 3H.

claim: In co-expressing cells, the particles associated with both KIF5B and KIF13B had speeds that were intermediate between those of KIF5B and KIF13B.
source: In 4X-KO cells where the two kinesins were expressed separately, this analysis showed that mCherry-Rab6A vesicles bound to KIF5B-GFP moved slower than the ones bound to GFP-KIF13B, whereas in co-expressing cells, the particles associated with both motors had speeds that were intermediate between those of KIF5B and KIF13B (Figure 4F,G), in agreement with the data on the recruitment of these two motors to peroxisomes (Figure 3H).
evidence: The text states this observation from automated speed analysis and refers to Figure 4F,G and Figure 3H.

claim: The projected distances between KIF5B or KIF13B and Rab6 were strongly skewed toward positive values, with a median value of 76 and 56 nm, respectively.
source: In contrast, the projected distances between KIF5B or KIF13B and Rab6 were strongly skewed toward positive values, with a median value of 76 and 56 nm, respectively (Figure 5G).
evidence: The text states this quantification from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5G showing histograms.

claim: The angles between the line connecting the centers of the two fluorescent signals and the velocity vector were distributed randomly when the positions of Rab6 and PAUF were analyzed.
source: The angles between the line connecting the centers of the two fluorescent signals (the distance vector) and the velocity vector (angle α, Figure 5F) were distributed randomly when the positions of Rab6 and PAUF were analyzed.
evidence: The text states this observation from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5F.

claim: In the case of Rab6 and the two kinesins, the angles close to zero predominated, as can be expected if the kinesins were accumulating at the front of the moving vesicles.
source: In contrast, in the case of Rab6 and the two kinesins, the angles close to zero predominated, as can be expected if the kinesins were accumulating at the front of the moving vesicles (Figure 5H).
evidence: The text states this observation and interpretation from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5H showing angle distributions.

claim: The maximal projected distance between Rab6 and KIF5B or KIF13B signals observed for a given vesicle varied from a few tens of nanometers to ~500 nm.
source: Analysis of individual vesicles showed that the maximal projected distance between Rab6 and KIF5B or KIF13B signals observed for a given vesicle varied from a few tens of nanometers to ~500 nm (Figure 5I), as expected given that vesicles can have different sizes.
evidence: The text states this observation from individual vesicle analysis and refers to Figure 5I showing plots.

claim: Smaller vesicles are generated when the 4X-KO cells are rescued with KIF13B compared to KIF5B.
source: Since the average projected distances between KIF13B and Rab6 signals were smaller than those between KIF5B and Rab6 signals (Figure 5G), it appears that smaller vesicles are generated when the 4X-KO cells are rescued with KIF13B compared to KIF5B.
evidence: The text states this interpretation based on projected distance measurements and refers to Figure 5G.

claim: Vesicles detected by imaging PAUF and Rab6 were in the same size range as those found in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF5B, whereas vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF13B were smaller.
source: Importantly, vesicles detected by imaging PAUF and Rab6, without overexpressing any motors, were in the same size range as those found in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF5B, whereas vesicles in 4X-KO cells rescued with KIF13B were smaller (Figure 5J).
evidence: The text states this observation from distance measurements and refers to Figure 5J showing histograms.

claim: More vesicles with larger areas were observed when 4X-KO cells were rescued with KIF5B compared to KIF13B.
source: In addition, more vesicles with larger areas were observed when 4X-KO cells were rescued with KIF5B compared to KIF13B (Figure 5K).
evidence: The text states this observation from vesicle area measurements and refers to Figure 5K showing histograms.

claim: KIF5B is important for controlling vesicle size, a function that cannot be compensated by KIF13B.
source: These data suggest that KIF5B, which is normally the main motor transporting Rab6 vesicles, is important for controlling vesicle size, a function that cannot be compensated by KIF13B, possibly because it performs less well under hindering load (Arpağ et al., 2019; Arpağ et al., 2014).
evidence: The text states this interpretation based on vesicle size measurements and cites previous work on motor properties under load.

claim: When KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B were colocalized on the same moving particle, KIF5B was shifted to the rear compared to KIF13B.
source: Next, we compared the distribution of KIF5B-GFP and mCherry-KIF13B when they were colocalized on the same moving particle (Figure 5G,H, green line). Interestingly, in this situation, KIF5B was shifted to the rear compared to KIF13B, which would be consistent with the idea that KIF5B, which is slower and has a lower detachment probability under load (Arpağ et al., 2019; Arpağ et al., 2014), exerts a drag force, whereas the faster KIF13B accumulates at the front of the vesicle.
evidence: The text states this observation from sub-pixel localization analysis and refers to Figure 5G,H, citing previous work on motor properties.

claim: For backward runs, the average displacement was close to zero for KIF13B (~3.5 nm) and was slightly negative (~ - 34.1 nm) for KIF5B.
source: Interestingly, for the backward runs, the average displacement was close to zero for KIF13B (~3.5 nm) and was slightly negative (~ - 34.1 nm) for KIF5B (Figure 5M).
evidence: The text states this quantification from analysis of opposite polarity runs and refers to Figure 5M showing plots.

claim: When a vesicle switches to dynein-driven motility, KIF13B does not undergo any tug-of-war with dynein, whereas KIF5B might be exerting some hindering force.
source: These data suggest that when a vesicle switches to dynein-driven motility, KIF13B does not undergo any tug-of-war with dynein, whereas KIF5B might be exerting some hindering force.
evidence: The text states this interpretation based on the analysis of opposite polarity runs showing different projected distances for KIF13B and KIF5B during backward runs.

claim: Both kinesins can actively engage on the vesicle when it moves toward MT plus end, but only KIF5B can oppose dynein.
source: Overall, our sub-pixel localization analysis suggests that both kinesins can actively engage on the vesicle when it moves toward MT plus end, but only KIF5B can oppose dynein.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on sub-pixel localization analysis of forward and backward runs.

claim: Partial depletion of KIF5B did not have a major effect on the overall secretion of neuropeptide Y (NPY).
source: Previous work showed that partial depletion of KIF5B did not have a major effect on the overall secretion of neuropeptide Y (NPY), a soluble cargo present in Rab6 vesicles (Grigoriev et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Grigoriev et al., 2007) for this claim.

claim: The surface staining of E-Cadherin-GFP in 4X-KO cells was similar to that in control cells one hour after the addition of biotin in the RUSH assay.
source: One hour after the addition of biotin, the surface staining of GFP in 4X-KO cells was similar to that in control cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text states this observation from the RUSH assay and flow cytometry analysis and refers to Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: No difference in the secretion of soluble-GFP was observed two hours after biotin addition in control versus 4X-KO cells.
source: We did not observe any difference in the secretion of soluble-GFP two hours after biotin addition (Figure 6D).
evidence: The text states this observation from the RUSH assay and flow cytometry analysis and refers to Figure 6D.

claim: No significant differences in the number of exocytotic events were observed in the 4X-KO compared to control cells.
source: We did not observe significant differences in the number of exocytotic events in the 4X-KO compared to control cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: The text states this observation from NPY-GFP exocytosis analysis and refers to Figure 6F showing quantification.

claim: In control cells, NPY-GFP exocytotic events were distributed along the entire radius of the cell, with many events at the cell periphery.
source: However, whereas in control cells these events were distributed along the entire radius of the cell, with many events at the cell periphery, in 4X-KO cells exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi (Figure 6G).
evidence: The text states this observation from spatial distribution analysis and refers to Figure 6G showing schematic and histogram.

claim: In 4X-KO cells, NPY-GFP exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi.
source: However, whereas in control cells these events were distributed along the entire radius of the cell, with many events at the cell periphery, in 4X-KO cells exocytotic events were restricted to the vicinity of the Golgi (Figure 6G).
evidence: The text states this observation from spatial distribution analysis and refers to Figure 6G showing schematic and histogram.

claim: Kinesin-driven Rab6-vesicle transport is not essential for secretion efficiency, but it is required for the correct spatial distribution of exocytotic events.
source: Kinesin-driven Rab6-vesicle transport is thus not essential for secretion efficiency, but it is required for the correct spatial distribution of exocytotic events.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the RUSH assay and NPY exocytosis analysis showing normal secretion levels but altered spatial distribution in 4X-KO cells.

claim: KIF5B depends on the members of MAP7 family for its activation.
source: Previous work has shown that KIF5B depends on the members of MAP7 family for its activation (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019), while kinesin-3 is inhibited by MAP7 (Monroy et al., 2018; Monroy et al., 2020).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019) for this claim.

claim: Kinesin-3 is inhibited by MAP7.
source: Previous work has shown that KIF5B depends on the members of MAP7 family for its activation (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019), while kinesin-3 is inhibited by MAP7 (Monroy et al., 2018; Monroy et al., 2020).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Monroy et al., 2018; Monroy et al., 2020) for this claim.

claim: The number of Rab6 vesicle runs was not significantly affected in MAP7-KO cells, but it was significantly reduced in cells lacking all MAP7 proteins.
source: The number of Rab6 vesicle runs was not significantly affected in MAP7-KO cells, but it was significantly reduced in cells lacking all MAP7 proteins (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: The text states this observation from tracking analysis and refers to Figure 7B,C showing tracking and quantification.

claim: The speed of Rab6 vesicle movement was similar in control and MAP7-KO cells, but increased in cells lacking all MAP7 proteins.
source: The speed of Rab6 vesicle movement was similar in control and MAP7-KO cells, but increased in cells lacking all MAP7 proteins (Figure 7D), consistent with the results obtained in KIF5B-KO cells (Figure 3A–D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The text states this observation from speed analysis and refers to Figure 7D and Figure 3A–D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The MAP7/tubulin intensity ratio decreases along the cell radius.
source: Simultaneous labeling of MTs with antibodies against α-tubulin and MAP7, MAP7D1 or MAP7D3 showed that the MAP7/tubulin intensity ratio decreases along the cell radius (Figure 8A), and this distribution was not affected by the knockout of KIF5B (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), indicating that transport driven by this kinesin has no detectable effect on the localization of these MAPs.
evidence: The text states this observation from immunofluorescence analysis and refers to Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The distribution of MAP7 proteins was not affected by the knockout of KIF5B.
source: Simultaneous labeling of MTs with antibodies against α-tubulin and MAP7, MAP7D1 or MAP7D3 showed that the MAP7/tubulin intensity ratio decreases along the cell radius (Figure 8A), and this distribution was not affected by the knockout of KIF5B (Figure 8—figure supplement 1), indicating that transport driven by this kinesin has no detectable effect on the localization of these MAPs.
evidence: The text states this observation from immunofluorescence analysis and refers to Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increase of Rab6 vesicle velocity observed in cells lacking MAP7 proteins was more pronounced in the center of the cell compared to the cell periphery.
source: Indeed, the increase of Rab6 vesicle velocity observed in cells lacking MAP7 proteins was more pronounced in the center of the cell compared to the cell periphery (Figure 8B).
evidence: The text states this observation from spatial velocity analysis and refers to Figure 8B showing velocity versus distance from Golgi.

claim: The absence of KIF13B led to a decrease in Rab6 vesicle speed at the cell margin.
source: Furthermore, the absence of KIF13B, the faster motor, led to a decrease in Rab6 vesicle speed at the cell margin (Figure 8B), where the contribution of this motor would be expected to be more substantial.
evidence: The text states this observation from spatial velocity analysis and refers to Figure 8B.

claim: Overexpression of KIF13B in the 4X-KO cell line led to an increase in Rab6 vesicle speed along the cell radius.
source: Conversely, overexpression of KIF13B in the 4X-KO cell line led to an increase in Rab6 vesicle speed along the cell radius.
evidence: The text states this observation, which is supported by data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: MAP7 displays a delay in binding to freshly grown, EB3-positive MT ends.
source: Indeed, live cell imaging showed that MAP7 displays a delay in binding to freshly grown, EB3-positive MT ends (Figure 8C,D).
evidence: The text states this observation from live cell imaging and refers to Figure 8C,D showing kymographs and quantification.

claim: KIF5B-560 was significantly less abundant on EB3-positive MT ends compared to older, EB3-negative MT lattices.
source: Also KIF5B followed this localization pattern: the dimeric motor fragment KIF5B-560 was significantly less abundant on EB3-positive MT ends compared to older, EB3-negative MT lattices (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: The text states this observation from live cell imaging and refers to Figure 8E,F showing kymographs and quantification.

claim: The motor domain containing fragment of KIF13B, KIF13B-380, which was dimerized by fusing it to a leucine zipper, was enriched at the growing MT ends.
source: In contrast, the motor domain containing fragment of KIF13B, KIF13B-380, which was dimerized by fusing it to a leucine zipper, was enriched at the growing MT ends (Figure 8G,H).
evidence: The text states this observation from live cell imaging and refers to Figure 8G,H showing kymographs and quantification.

claim: In the absence of KIF13B, Rab6 vesicles are less efficient in reaching the newly grown, EB3 positive MT ends.
source: Based on these results, we hypothesized that in the absence of KIF13B, Rab6 vesicles will be less efficient in reaching the newly grown, EB3 positive MT ends and found that this was indeed the case (Figure 8I,J).
evidence: The text states this hypothesis and observation from colocalization analysis and refers to Figure 8I,J showing images and quantification.

claim: The combined action of KIF5B and KIF13B allows Rab6 vesicles to efficiently navigate different MT populations.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that the combined action of KIF5B and KIF13B allows Rab6 vesicles to efficiently navigate different MT populations.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the spatial analysis of vesicle speeds and motor localization on different MT populations.

claim: MAP7 proteins contribute to the spatial regulation of exocytotic vesicle transport by promoting the activation of KIF5B and possibly by inhibiting KIF13B on older MTs.
source: MAP7 proteins contribute to the spatial regulation of exocytotic vesicle transport by promoting the activation of KIF5B and possibly by inhibiting KIF13B on older MTs.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the analysis of MAP7 distribution, its effect on vesicle speeds, and previous work on MAP7's effects on kinesins.

claim: Rab6 represents a robust marker of a broad variety of post-Golgi carriers.
source: Rab6 represents a robust marker of a broad variety of post-Golgi carriers (Fourriere et al., 2019; Grigoriev et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Fourriere et al., 2019; Grigoriev et al., 2007) for this claim.

claim: The composition of motors controlling Rab6 vesicle motility is expected to be cell type-specific.
source: Such vesicles are likely to be heterogeneous, and the composition of motors controlling their motility is expected to be cell type-specific.
evidence: The text states this as an expectation based on the heterogeneity of Rab6 vesicles.

claim: KIF1A/B/C family is involved in the transport of Rab6-positive carriers in neurons and Vero cells.
source: Indeed, our previous work established the involvement of KIF1A/B/C family in the transport of Rab6-positive carriers in neurons and Vero cells (Gumy et al., 2017; Schlager et al., 2010).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Gumy et al., 2017; Schlager et al., 2010) for this claim.

claim: KIF5B was recently shown to be bound to different membranes including Rab6 vesicles by the Dopey1-Mon2 complex, which functions as a lipid-regulated cargo-adaptor.
source: KIF5B was recently shown to be bound to different membranes including Rab6 vesicles by the Dopey1-Mon2 complex, which functions as a lipid-regulated cargo-adaptor (Mahajan et al., 2019).
evidence: The text cites recent work (Mahajan et al., 2019) for this claim.

claim: KIF1C was shown to interact with Rab6-positive membranes directly.
source: KIF1C was shown to interact with Rab6-positive membranes directly (Lee et al., 2015) and also by associating with a cell-specific adaptor protein BICDR-1, which is absent from HeLa cells (Schlager et al., 2010).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Lee et al., 2015; Schlager et al., 2010) for this claim.

claim: BICDR-1 is absent from HeLa cells.
source: KIF1C was shown to interact with Rab6-positive membranes directly (Lee et al., 2015) and also by associating with a cell-specific adaptor protein BICDR-1, which is absent from HeLa cells (Schlager et al., 2010).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Schlager et al., 2010) for this claim.

claim: It is possible that the adaptor complexes for KIF5B and KIF13B on Rab6 vesicles have some overlapping components, similar to lysosomes.
source: It is possible that the adaptor complexes for KIF5B and KIF13B on Rab6 vesicles have some overlapping components, similar to lysosomes, where the BORC/Arl8 complex recruits KIF5B through the interaction with SKIP and KLC and binds to kinesin-3 KIF1A/B directly, through the interaction with the coiled-coil domains of the motors (Guardia et al., 2016).
evidence: The text states this as a possibility and cites previous work (Guardia et al., 2016) on lysosome adaptor complexes.

claim: Spatial segregation of KIF5B and KIF13B present on the same vesicles suggests that they are not part of the same molecular complex.
source: However, spatial segregation of KIF5B and KIF13B present on the same vesicles (see below) suggests that they are not part of the same molecular complex.
evidence: The text states this interpretation based on the sub-pixel localization data showing different positions of the two kinesins on vesicles.

claim: The higher resistance of KIF5B to detachment under load is thought to be the main determinant of motor behavior in a mixture of motors.
source: The higher resistance of KIF5B to detachment under load, which is thought to be the main determinant of motor behavior in a mixture of motors (Arpağ et al., 2014), also likely contributes to this distribution.
evidence: The text cites previous work (Arpağ et al., 2014) for this claim.

claim: The reported interaction between KIF5B and the dynein adaptor BICD2 could in principle control the localization of this kinesin on the vesicle.
source: The reported interaction between KIF5B and the dynein adaptor BICD2 (Grigoriev et al., 2007) or some additional interactions between KIF5B and the dynein-dynactin complex could in principle control the localization of this kinesin on the vesicle.
evidence: The text states this as a possibility and cites previous work (Grigoriev et al., 2007) on the KIF5B-BICD2 interaction.

claim: The data are incompatible with the idea that KIF5B and dynein are part of the same protein complexes on secretory vesicles.
source: Importantly, we find that KIF5B tends to move to the rear of the vesicle when it switches directions and is presumably driven to MT minus ends by cytoplasmic dynein. These data are incompatible with the idea that KIF5B and dynein are part of the same protein complexes on secretory vesicles.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the observation that KIF5B moves to the rear during direction reversal.

claim: Drug-mediated MT disassembly does not block post-Golgi trafficking.
source: In line with previous work showing that drug-mediated MT disassembly does not block post-Golgi trafficking (Fourriere et al., 2016; Hirschberg et al., 1998; Rindler et al., 1987; Rogalski et al., 1984; Van De Moortele et al., 1993), we found that the efficiency of secretion was normal is cells lacking four kinesins.
evidence: The text cites previous work (Fourriere et al., 2016; Hirschberg et al., 1998; Rindler et al., 1987; Rogalski et al., 1984; Van De Moortele et al., 1993) for this claim.

claim: Kinesin-1 contributes to the generation of Rab6 vesicles by pulling membrane tubules before their fission from the Golgi apparatus.
source: Previous work suggested that kinesin-1 contributes to the generation of Rab6 vesicles by pulling membrane tubules before their fission from the Golgi apparatus (Miserey-Lenkei et al., 2010).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Miserey-Lenkei et al., 2010) for this claim.

claim: Such contribution of kinesin-1 to vesicle formation is not essential for the formation of secretory carriers.
source: While our data indicate that such contribution is not essential for the formation of secretory carriers, we did find that Rab6 vesicles generated in the presence of KIF13B alone were smaller than those formed when KIF5B was also expressed.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the observation that secretion efficiency is normal in 4X-KO cells.

claim: In HeLa cells, Rab6 vesicles preferentially fuse with the plasma membrane at the cell periphery in the vicinity of focal adhesions.
source: An obvious function of kinesins in secretory vesicle transport, confirmed by our work, is the control of the spatial distribution of exocytosis events. In HeLa cells, Rab6 vesicles preferentially fuse with the plasma membrane at the cell periphery in the vicinity of focal adhesions (Fourriere et al., 2019; Grigoriev et al., 2007; Stehbens et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Fourriere et al., 2019; Grigoriev et al., 2007; Stehbens et al., 2014) for this claim.

claim: Exocytosis preferentially occurs at the sites where dynamic MT plus ends are attached to the cell cortex by the complex of CLASPs, LL5β, KANK1 and ELKS, which together with MICAL3 regulates vesicle fusion.
source: Exocytosis preferentially occurs at the sites where dynamic MT plus ends are attached to the cell cortex by the complex of CLASPs, LL5β, KANK1 and ELKS, which together with MICAL3 regulates vesicle fusion (Grigoriev et al., 2011; Lansbergen et al., 2006).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Grigoriev et al., 2011; Lansbergen et al., 2006) for this claim.

claim: Spatial organization of exocytosis can contribute to cell migration by directing secretion of new membrane and extracellular matrix proteins to the leading edge of the cell and also by controlling focal adhesion turnover.
source: Such spatial organization can contribute to cell migration by directing secretion of new membrane and extracellular matrix proteins to the leading edge of the cell and also by controlling focal adhesion turnover (Schmoranzer et al., 2000; Stehbens et al., 2014).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Schmoranzer et al., 2000; Stehbens et al., 2014) for this claim.

claim: Cargo unloading at dynamic MT ends could be a general property of kinesin-3 family members.
source: Our data suggest that KIF13B, being a minor player in Rab6 vesicle transport in HeLa cells, likely due to its low abundance, nevertheless contributes to the spatial organization of exocytosis by bringing the vesicles to the tips of dynamic MTs. Cargo unloading at dynamic MT ends could be a general property of kinesin-3 family members, as it was also recently proposed for KIF1A (Guedes-Dias et al., 2019).
evidence: The text states this as a possibility and cites recent work (Guedes-Dias et al., 2019) on KIF1A.

claim: KIF5B is restricted to the older, more stable MT population.
source: KIF5B, which strongly dominates Rab6 vesicle transport, is in contrast restricted to the older, more stable MT population (Cai et al., 2009; Guardia et al., 2016; Tas et al., 2017).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Cai et al., 2009; Guardia et al., 2016; Tas et al., 2017) for this claim.

claim: The mechanisms of kinesin-1 selectivity are complex, and might involve the ability of the motor to regulate the properties of the tracks on which it walks.
source: The underlying mechanisms of kinesin-1 selectivity are complex, and might involve the ability of the motor to regulate the properties of the tracks on which it walks (Shima et al., 2018).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Shima et al., 2018) for this claim.

claim: MAP7 family members control both kinesin recruitment to the MT and its activation.
source: Importantly, KIF5B shows a very strong dependence on MAP7 family members, which control both kinesin recruitment to the MT and its activation (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Hooikaas et al., 2019; Metzger et al., 2012; Monroy et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2019) for this claim.

claim: In COS7 cells, overexpressed GFP-MAP7 was reported to form a sharp boundary along the MT shaft, associated with the end of the stable MT segment.
source: In COS7 cells, where MTs are more dynamic than in the HeLa cells studied here, overexpressed GFP-MAP7 was reported to form a sharp boundary along the MT shaft, associated with the end of the stable MT segment (Tymanskyj and Ma, 2019).
evidence: The text cites previous work (Tymanskyj and Ma, 2019) for this claim.

claim: In cells with highly dynamic MTs, Rab6 transport to MT plus ends will be more dependent on kinesin-3 family members.
source: It can be expected that in cells with highly dynamic MTs, Rab6 transport to MT plus ends will be more dependent on kinesin-3 family members.
evidence: The text states this as an expectation based on the observation that MAP7 is slow to populate new MT ends and KIF5B depends on MAP7.

claim: KIF13B can work well not only on freshly polymerized but also on older, MAP7-positive MTs.
source: Interestingly, since KIF13B expression is able to rescue Rab6 vesicle transport in the absence of KIF5B, and the distribution of MAP7 family members is not affected by KIF5B loss, it appears that KIF13B can work well not only on freshly polymerized but also on older, MAP7-positive MTs, even though the motility of kinesin-3 has been shown to be negatively affected by MAP7 (Monroy et al., 2020).
evidence: The text states this interpretation based on rescue experiments and cites previous work (Monroy et al., 2020) on MAP7's effect on kinesin-3.

claim: The expression of MAP7 proteins in HeLa cells is sufficient to support transport by kinesin-1 but not to hinder KIF13B activity.
source: The expression of MAP7 proteins in HeLa cells is thus sufficient to support transport by kinesin-1 but not to hinder KIF13B activity.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the observation that KIF13B can rescue vesicle transport in the absence of KIF5B despite the presence of MAP7.

claim: Additional MAPs promoting kinesin-3 motility may allow KIF13B to move on MTs in spite of the presence of MAP7 family members.
source: Alternatively, additional MAPs promoting kinesin-3 motility may allow KIF13B to move on MTs in spite of the presence of MAP7 family members.
evidence: The text states this as an alternative explanation for how KIF13B can function on MAP7-positive MTs.
